caption: Adjust: a scrolling palette with its hue turned slowly round the wheel and its saturation boosted
why: Once a colour is made, you often want it a bit different: warmer, paler, punchier, the opposite. Adjust is the photo-editing panel for one colour - turn the hue, raise or drain the saturation, brighten, add contrast, bend the mids with gamma, or invert.

Because it works on whatever colour comes in, it is the easy way to vary a whole effect: one Adjust before the Output changes everything. Its neighbours: Levels is just brightness, contrast and gamma; Scale and Fade only dim; HSV builds a colour from hue, saturation and value; Adjust changes one you already have.
steps: The usual scrolling palette - **Speed** times **Time**, plus **Coords** `u`, into a **Palette**'s index - goes into Adjust's **color**.
**hue** comes from a slow clock (**Time** times 0.1): every colour is turned round the wheel, a tenth of a turn a second, so the whole palette drifts through other hues.

**saturation** is 1.4: colours a little more vivid than the palette's own. **value** (1) is a brightness multiplier, **contrast** (1) pushes toward black and white above 1, **gamma** (1) lifts the mids below 1.
**invert** is off. The adjusted colour goes to the **Output**.

try.label: Invert
try.text: invert on: every colour becomes its opposite - red to cyan, blue to yellow.

try.label: Greyscale
try.text: saturation 0: all colour drained, only brightness left.

try.label: Punchy
try.text: contrast 2 and gamma 0.6: darks pushed down, brights up, mids lifted - a harder, more saturated look.
